brief.title: Pipeline review with Nadia, VP Sales

go.text: Halden Mutual: grant 19% off, or hold the price?

in_mind.text: She has raised the Halden Mutual discount in 3 of the last 4 reviews.

brief.briefing:
Help me prepare my 08:45 pipeline review with Nadia, VP Sales.

What I know so far, from this morning’s brief:
- She has raised the Halden Mutual discount in 3 of the last 4 reviews.
- Halden Mutual want 19% off. Bergen asked the same in July; I held, and it closed at 79k.

That is a starting point, not the agenda. Start with the Halden Mutual procurement thread from 10 September and #deals-emea, then look at our recent exchanges and past reviews with fresh eyes. Tell me the topics likely to come up, the decisions to make, what Nadia wants from me, and the context I should have in mind, including anything the brief did not see. Then ask me where I want to go deeper.

in_mind.text: She has chased the renewal playbook 3 times.

brief.briefing:
Help me prepare my 10:00 one to one with Elena, Head of Customer Success, six months in.

- I have moved this meeting twice.
- She has chased the renewal playbook three times. Her last message was not a question, it said the playbook ships without me.
- Nothing to land. She sets the agenda.

That is a starting point, not the agenda. Start with her recent Slack messages to me, then look at our exchanges and past one to ones with fresh eyes. Tell me the topics likely to come up, what she wants from me underneath the playbook chase, and the context I should have in mind, including anything the brief did not see. Then ask me where I want to go deeper.

in_mind.text: The room has picked October twice.

brief.briefing:
Help me prepare the 11:00 migration go or no go. 45 minutes, six people, Tomas chairing.

- Slipped from 28 August. The room has picked October twice.
- To land: the 4 October weekend, or November.

That is a starting point, not the agenda. Start with Tomas’s migration plan v3 and #infra-migration, then look at the other threads on the migration with fresh eyes. Tell me the topics likely to come up, the decisions to make, what each person in the room wants, and the context I should have in mind, including anything the brief did not see. Then ask me where I want to go deeper.

decisions.say: Halden Mutual: grant 19% off, or hold the price?
argument: Bergen asked the same in July: you held, it closed at 79k.
decisions.briefing:
Help me decide on Halden Mutual’s discount: grant 19% off, or hold the price.

From this morning’s brief:
- Halden Mutual want 19% off. Nadia, VP Sales, wants to give it.
- Bergen asked for the same discount in July. I held, and it closed at 79k eleven days later.

Read the Halden Mutual procurement thread from 10 September and the Bergen thread from July yourself. Then give me the case for each side, what each one does to the renewals that come after it, and anything else that bears on it, an option I have not listed included. Do not send anything.

decisions.say: Migration: the 4 October weekend, or November?
decisions.briefing:
Help me decide the migration date: the 4 October weekend, or November. I have to call it at 11:00.

From this morning’s brief:
- November lands inside the renewal cycle for nine accounts.
- Elena has been told neither date.
- Support needs a week to staff whichever I pick.

Read #infra-migration and pull the nine November renewals from the calendar yourself. Then lay out the two dates side by side on the things that actually differ: renewal exposure, how much notice support gets, and what breaks if it slips again. Tell me anything else that bears on it, a third date included if there is one.

argument: The same sections were missing last quarter: you wrote them the night before.
decisions.briefing:
Help me decide how to finish the board pack for Thursday: cut a section, or write all five.

From this morning’s brief:
- Two of five sections exist.
- The same sections were missing last quarter, and I wrote them the night before.

Read the Q3 board pack and Marc’s outline yourself. Then tell me what each option costs, which section the board would miss least if one goes, and any other way through I have not listed.

argument: Promised for this morning: the 4th date she has been given.
jobs.briefing:
Help me sign off Elena’s renewal playbook before I see her at 10:00.

From this morning’s brief:
- Elena asked three times. Her last message was not a question, it said the playbook ships without me.

Read playbook v4 and her Slack messages yourself. Then do two things. Tell me the three decisions in it that actually need me, ignoring everything that does not. And draft my sign-off note: approves it, owns the delay without grovelling, and flags only what genuinely needs changing.

argument: All 4 are in last quarter's cohort view.
jobs.briefing:
Send Julien the cohort numbers before 14:00.

From this morning’s brief:
- Last quarter I went into board prep without them and spent the session reconstructing the numbers out loud.
- Board prep is at 14:00 today.

Read Julien’s request and the Q3 cohort model yourself. Pull the numbers he actually asked for, sanity check them against the model, and draft the mail. Numbers in the body, not attached. Flag anything that looks wrong before I send it.

jobs.say: Give Priya the Q4 roadmap order.
argument: She is waiting on your answer to Nadia about Halden Mutual.
jobs.briefing:
Give Priya the Q4 roadmap order. She asked on 3 September.

From this morning’s brief:
- This has slipped every week since 25 August. It waits on me, not on Priya.
- It unblocks the moment the Halden Mutual discount is settled.

Read Priya’s 3 September message and the draft order yourself. Then tell me which parts of the ordering genuinely depend on the Halden Mutual outcome and which I could confirm to her today regardless. Draft the reply that unblocks her on everything that is not actually blocked.
